newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Senate panel suspends vote on Banerj deal.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Senate panel suspends vote on Banerj deal.

text.p: The session of a Senate committee due to vote on a deal resolving pension-related debts of Rio de Janeiro state bank Banerj was suspended, an official said.
"The session was suspended because the committee failed to gather enough senators to vote," an official at the Senate's Economic Affairs Committee said.
Only 10 senators of the 14 necessary were ready to vote, he added.
The official said the session could be rescheduled for later Tuesday.
"The meeting may be set for later today," he said.

Government leaders in the Senate may also send a motion requesting that the Banerj deal be made a priority so that it may be put for a vote in the floor of the upper house without prior approval from the panel, he added.

Banerj is scheduled to be auctioned off at 1400 local/1700 GMT Tuesday on the Rio de Janeiro Stock Exchange, but Senate approval of the deal is key to allow the state to go ahead with its plans to sell the bank.
The Senate must approve a 2.9 billion reais loan from federal mortgage bank Caixa Economica Federal (CEF) which will cover all of Banerj's pension and payroll-related debts.
Also a court injunction granted by a state judge suspending the sale still has to be revoked.
